data.title: CIVIL RIGHTS ORGANIZATION ALLEGES MAJOR TELEHEALTH PROVIDERS EXCLUDE DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING COMMUNITIES NATIONWIDE
data.description:
CIVIL RIGHTS ORGANIZATION ALLEGES MAJOR TELEHEALTH PROVIDERS EXCLUDE DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING COMMUNITIES NATIONWIDE

CIVIL RIGHTS ORGANIZATION ALLEGES MAJOR TELEHEALTH PROVIDERS EXCLUDE DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING COMMUNITIES NATIONWIDE

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Nov. 19, 2026

Equal Rights Center lawsuits claim MedStar, VitaLink, and Sesame fail to provide ASL interpretation and/or live captioning for d/Deaf and hard of hearing patients

WASHINGTON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, the Equal Rights Center (ERC) announced lawsuits against three telehealth providers—MedStar Health, Inc. (MedStar), VitaLink Telehealth LLC (VitaLink), and Sesame, Inc. (Sesame)—alleging that they fail to provide effective communication for d/Deaf* and hard of hearing individuals. Specifically, the complaints—which were filed in D.C. Superior Court—allege that MedStar excludes deaf and hard of hearing patients by not offering live captioning for telehealth visits, VitaLink excludes Deaf patients by not offering American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation, and Sesame excludes both groups by not offering ASL interpretation or live captioning.

"After ERC members reported concerns about telehealth accessibility, we conducted civil rights testing that identified wide-ranging violations of accessibility requirements designed to ensure effective communication for d/Deaf and hard of hearing people," remarks ERC Executive Director Kate Scott. "Telehealth promises to make medical care more accessible, but our investigation found that providers are effectively closing their doors to d/Deaf and hard of hearing patients."

Through the complaints, ERC alleges that MedStar, VitaLink, and Sesame violate the D.C. Human Rights Act by discriminating against people with disabilities and the D.C. Consumer Protection Procedures Act by falsely claiming to be accessible. While the lawsuits are based in Washington, D.C., the cases have far-reaching implications. MedStar conducted more than 500,000 telehealth visits in Fiscal Year 2025 for patients across D.C., Maryland, and northern Virginia. VitaLink serves 15 states plus Washington, D.C. Sesame operates in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C. and has reportedly treated more than 500,000 patients.

Accessible health care is of critical importance to people with disabilities. Telehealth visits give patients the ability to see medical providers online without the burden of traveling to an office. However, for d/Deaf and hard of hearing individuals, a telehealth visit is only as accessible as the platform on which it takes place.

Deaf individuals who communicate using ASL cannot participate in telehealth visits conducted in English unless an ASL interpreter is present. Likewise, deaf and hard of hearing individuals who rely on live captioning cannot effectively participate in telehealth visits without it. ASL interpretation is not an appropriate substitute for live captioning, nor is live captioning an appropriate substitute for ASL interpretation.

Effective communication is especially important in medical settings. Visits often involve precise and nuanced conversations about a patient's symptoms, medical history, treatment options, and follow-up care. Patients have a right to participate fully in these conversations with their providers and make informed decisions, but that is often impossible for d/Deaf and hard of hearing individuals without proper accommodations.

Law firm Handley Farah & Anderson is representing ERC in the three lawsuits. Partner Martha Guarnieri comments, "Telehealth offers a lot of potential benefits, but it's useless to millions of patients if it's not accessible. We're proud to work with ERC to ensure d/Deaf and hard of hearing folks have equal access to these platforms."

The complaint against MedStar is available here.

The complaint against VitaLink is available here.

The complaint against Sesame is available here.

CONTACT:
Nick Adjami, Communications & Engagement Manager
Equal Rights Center
nadjami@equalrightscenter.org, (202) 370-3219

*The uppercase "Deaf" refers to a particular group of people who share a language (sign language) and a culture, or to one's identity within that group. The lowercase "deaf" is used in reference to the audiological condition of not hearing. People who use it to describe themselves might not identify as part of the uppercase Deaf community. In this press release, we use "d/Deaf" to refer to both categories.

ABOUT THE EQUAL RIGHTS CENTER: ERC advances equal access, opportunity, and fair treatment so individuals and communities can thrive. To achieve this mission, ERC uses complementary strategies that support individuals, expose discrimination, promote institutional accountability, prevent unfair treatment, and advance systemic change. Our deepest expertise is in fair housing and disability rights, but we also work in other areas, particularly where civil rights testing can help uncover discrimination and promote accountability. For more information, please visit www.equalrightscenter.org.

ABOUT HANDLEY FARAH & ANDERSON: Handley Farah & Anderson are lawyers who seek to improve the world. Based in Washington, D.C., they fight for: workers deprived of wages, consumers deceived about products, tenants denied access to housing, farmers mistreated by processors, parents deprived of adequate parental leave, investors who were defrauded, small businesses harmed by antitrust violations, persons with disabilities denied access, whistleblowers who uncover fraud, and women and communities of color subject to discrimination.

data.title: OCLC and Ecole Solutions partner to bring EZproxy services to libraries across India
data.description:
OCLC and Ecole Solutions partner to bring EZproxy services to libraries across India

OCLC and Ecole Solutions partner to bring EZproxy services to libraries across India

PR Newswire

DUBLIN, Ohio and BANGALORE, India, Nov. 19, 2026

Ecole Solutions is now OCLC's distributor for hosted EZproxy and EZproxy
Analytics, providing local sales, training, and support for Indian institutions

DUBLIN, Ohio and BANGALORE, India, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OCLC and Ecole Solutions, the Bangalore-based provider of technology solutions for libraries and academic institutions, today announced a distribution partnership to make OCLC's hosted EZproxy and EZproxy Analytics available to academic and research libraries in India.

 OCLC and Ecole Solutions are partnering to make OCLC's EZproxy available to academic and research libraries in India

Ecole Solutions will market and sell both services and provide local customer support, including implementation, training, and technical assistance. The distribution agreement covers much of the Indian subcontinent, including India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.

Designed around user privacy, EZproxy simply and securely connects students and researchers to electronic journal articles and other e-resources in a library's collection. Hosted EZproxy is OCLC's fully managed e-resource access and authentication service. It enables libraries to provide authorized users with access to licensed electronic resources using their existing institutional sign-on credentials. EZproxy Analytics complements COUNTER reporting by using powerful data exploration and visualization tools across EZproxy log files to make it easier to curate e-resources and prove their value.

"We're delighted to welcome Ecole Solutions as our partner in India," said Eric van Lubeek, Managing Director, OCLC EMEA/Asia Pacific. "Ecole Solutions' local knowledge and technical expertise will help libraries quickly implement and realize the benefits of EZproxy services. This partnership reflects our long-term commitment to supporting the Indian library community."

India's One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) initiative expands access to scholarly research publications across the country. At the same time, libraries continue to invest in databases, e-books, and other digital resources and need reliable information to assess their use and value.

"EZproxy works with virtually any publisher and alongside the national federations and institutional logins libraries already use, giving researchers one way into their collection, from anywhere," said L. S. Venkatesh, Director, Ecole Solutions. "Librarians gain the usage evidence they need for collection decisions and quality reviews. OCLC hosts the service, and our team provides local support."

OCLC and Ecole Solutions leaders will introduce the new partnership and meet with library leaders at the PLANNER 2026 Convention in Guwahati, India, 25-27 November.

Libraries in India interested in learning more can visit https://www.ecoleglobal.com/.

More about EZproxy is on the OCLC website.

About Ecole Solutions

Ecole Solutions is an India-based technology services provider specializing in digital transformation for educational institutions. It delivers advanced plagiarism and AI-detection software, alongside e-learning and campus management solutions. These tools empower universities nationwide to enforce strict academic integrity and optimize operations.

About OCLC

OCLC is a nonprofit global library organization that provides shared technology services, original research, and community programs so that libraries can better fuel learning, research, and innovation. Through OCLC, member libraries cooperatively produce and maintain WorldCat, the most comprehensive global network of data about library collections and services. Libraries gain efficiencies through OCLC's WorldShare, a complete set of library management applications and services built on an open, cloud-based platform. It is through collaboration and sharing of the world's collected knowledge that libraries can help people find answers they need to solve problems. Together as OCLC, member libraries, staff, and partners make breakthroughs possible.

OCLC, WorldCat, WorldShare, and EZproxy are trademarks and/or service marks of OCLC, Inc. Third-party product, service and business names are trademarks and/or service marks of their respective owners.

For more information: Contact Bob Murphy at murphyb@oclc.org or +1-614-761-5136

data.title: Mindr Leads Impaired Driving Conversation at Midwest Traffic Safety Conference
data.description:
Mindr Leads Impaired Driving Conversation at Midwest Traffic Safety Conference

Mindr Leads Impaired Driving Conversation at Midwest Traffic Safety Conference

PR Newswire

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026

Session examined a shifting safety landscape in which drinking declines while alcohol-related crash numbers persist and THC use grows; Mindr presented a holistic suite of technologies to tackle the impairment crisis.

Key Takeaways

  • Mindr joined 500 traffic safety professionals at the 2026 Midwest Traffic Safety Conference, hosted by the Midwest Center for Traffic Safety, Nov. 10-12 in Itasca, Illinois.
  • Mindr's session, "Impairment Is Changing: A Hands-On Look at Alcohol and THC Detection Technology," gave attendees a hands-on look at alcohol and THC detection technology. Crashes involving alcohol-impaired drivers still account for 30% of U.S. traffic deaths, while cannabis plays a growing role.
  • Kate Riley, general manager of Keepr and recenTHC, and Karen Sisson, Esq., senior vice president of government affairs at Mindr, led the session, and attendees saw demonstrations of Mindr's full suite of safety solutions, including the latest Intoxalock ignition interlock device, Keepr Alcohol Monitoring, the voluntary Keepr Drive device and the recenTHC oral fluid test.

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mindr, a national leader in substance detection, monitoring and safety technology, led a session on shifting impairment trends and demonstrated its alcohol and THC detection technology for 500 law enforcement officers, prosecutors and traffic safety professionals at the 2026 Midwest Traffic Safety Conference, hosted by the Midwest Center for Traffic Safety from Nov. 10-12 in Itasca, Illinois. The session explored why alcohol-impaired crashes still account for 30% of U.S. traffic deaths, while cannabis plays a growing role.

On Nov. 10, Kate Riley, general manager of Keepr and recenTHC, and Karen Sisson, Esq., senior vice president of government affairs at Mindr, led the session "Impairment Is Changing: A Hands-On Look at Alcohol and THC Detection Technology." They walked attendees through current impairment trends and what those trends mean for the technology and policy tools available to help combat impaired driving.

A persistent gap framed much of the session. The percentage of U.S. adults who say they consume alcohol has fallen to 54%, the lowest in Gallup's nearly 90-year trend, and it held at that record low in 2026. Yet an estimated 15.5 million Americans ages 16 and older reported driving under the influence of alcohol in the past year, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. In 2024, 11,904 people died in crashes in which at least one driver was alcohol-impaired, 30% of all traffic fatalities in the United States, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). That is one death every 44 minutes, and nearly 4 in 10 of those killed were someone other than the impaired driver, including passengers, other motorists and pedestrians.

Closer to home, the Illinois numbers follow the same pattern. In 2024, 338 people died in crashes involving an alcohol-impaired driver, or 29% of the state's 1,177 traffic deaths, according to NHTSA. That was up from 309 in 2015. In 236 of those deaths, or 20% of all Illinois traffic fatalities, at least one driver had a blood alcohol concentration of 0.15 or higher, nearly twice the legal limit. The Illinois Secretary of State reports that 87% of drivers arrested for DUI in the state are first-time offenders, and Mothers Against Drunk Driving reports that the average drunk driver has driven 80 times before their first arrest.

"Impaired driving remains one of the most stubborn challenges on our roads, and no single agency can solve it alone," said Marc Fisher, executive director of the Midwest Center for Traffic Safety. "This conference brings together the officers, prosecutors and safety professionals from across the country who work on this problem every day. Having partners like Mindr in the room sharing tools that help people plan ahead before they ever get behind the wheel adds an important piece to that effort."

Riley and Sisson also highlighted how impairment is shifting beyond alcohol to cannabis and other substances. In an NHTSA study of seriously or fatally injured road users, 56% tested positive for at least one potentially impairing substance, and cannabinoids (25%) were detected slightly more often than alcohol (23%). The findings point to a clear shift in impairment trends and a growing need for tools, including those that can detect alcohol and THC.

Mindr continues to address these impairment trends through technology innovation to fulfill its mission to keep people and communities safe. Its latest innovations include Keepr Drive, a proactive, in-vehicle accountability tool that requires a breath test before the car starts; Keepr Alcohol Monitoring, which helps courts, family law professionals and behavioral health programs document breath alcohol testing activity outside of a vehicle; and recenTHC, an oral fluid test in development designed to detect recent THC use, as cannabis plays a growing role in workplace safety and impaired driving.

At the conference, Mindr showcased its full suite of safety solutions, including the latest Intoxalock ignition interlock device, now rolling out in new states including Pennsylvania and New Jersey, with more to follow. Attendees also saw demonstrations of Keepr Drive and recenTHC, giving them a firsthand look at the alcohol and THC detection technology behind Mindr's newest tools.

Law enforcement agencies, courts and traffic safety organizations interested in Mindr's alcohol and THC detection technology can learn more at mindr.com.

Mindr brings nearly four decades of alcohol detection experience to this effort, from developing the fuel cell technology that set the standard for today's ignition interlock devices to building a national network of more than 6,000 service centers that puts that technology within reach of anyone who needs it. Today, the company continues to advance the industry through research, thought leadership and new product development.

"Americans are drinking less than ever, yet impaired driving still accounts for nearly a third of traffic deaths, both nationally and here in Illinois. As impairment extends beyond alcohol to cannabis and other substances, keeping pace takes current data, collaboration and continued innovation," said Kathy Boden Holland, chief executive officer of Mindr. "Thank you to the Midwest Center for Traffic Safety for creating a space where everyone working on this challenge can learn from the same data and from each other. We're proud to be part of that effort and to keep innovating toward our shared mission of keeping people and communities safe."

Mindr will continue to work with the Midwest Center for Traffic Safety to support educational and policy initiatives in Illinois designed to help combat impaired driving.

About Mindr
Mindr is a national leader in substance detection, monitoring and safety solutions. Its portfolio of trusted brands includes Intoxalock, Breathe Easy Insurance, Keepr, DUI.org, recenTHC and ADS Interlock. Mindr is focused on making communities safer through innovative technologies that empower individuals with the tools to make better decisions.

Learn more about Mindr by visiting mindr.com.

About the Midwest Center for Traffic Safety
At the Midwest Center for Traffic Safety, our mission is to reduce traffic-related fatalities and serious injuries across the region by implementing evidence-based strategies grounded in the Safe System approach. We aim to address the most pressing issues contributing to roadway deaths — impaired and distracted driving, speeding and lack of seat belt use — by advancing equitable education, enforcement, engineering and emergency response practices.

Through collaborative partnerships, data-driven research and community engagement, we strive to create safer, more resilient transportation systems for all users, especially the most vulnerable. Our work supports long-term cultural change and sustainable improvements in road safety, ensuring that every journey, regardless of mode, age, income or background, is safe.

Media Assets: A full press kit from the conference, including photos and B-roll of Mindr's safety solutions and the in-vehicle Keepr Drive demonstration, is available here.

data.title: We're in our 50s and terrified of a market crash. Should we put $400,000 of our $1 million retirement savings into an annuity?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have a house worth $450,000. Our combined annual income is $125,000.'

"We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm wondering what your thoughts are on putting our house and other assets into a trust. Could it help reduce taxes or protect our assets from lawsuits, bankruptcy or other unforeseen circumstances? If so, what are the potential downsides or pitfalls?

We have a house worth $450,000 and about $1 million in retirement assets held in various qualified accounts. I'd also be interested in your thoughts on annuities for capital preservation and guaranteed income.

Would it make sense to put $400,000 of our $1 million in qualified retirement accounts into an annuity that would begin paying out at age 65, guaranteeing us $40,000 a year for life, while leaving the remaining $600,000 invested in a brokerage account for capital appreciation?

My spouse and I are 55 and 54, respectively. We're both working and plan to continue until 65. We're terrified of a market crash. We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000.

Curious in the Midwest

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'Nvidia has me spooked ': Should I sell my stocks or buy real estate?

That money you invest in an annuity is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Dear Curious,

I'll outline the advantages of your proposal - and then move on to the cons.

First, the pros of putting your money in an annuity, I presume, are to find a haven for part of your nest egg, albeit at a potentially lower rate than the stock market could provide. If you moved $400,000 from traditional 401(k)s or IRAs into an IRA annuity, the transaction generally would not trigger income taxes or the 10% early-withdrawal penalty, provided the funds are transferred correctly. A direct trustee-to-trustee transfer is typically the simplest approach. If you were selling $400,000 worth of investments in an ordinary brokerage account, however, you could owe capital-gains taxes on any profits realized from the sale.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security, which you presumably plan to take when you reach full retirement age. What you receive depends on the type of annuity: your initial investment, the interest rate or other terms you lock in and, of course, the payment schedule. Payouts can also vary with your age, your sex and whether the product is a joint-life annuity. If you expect to live a long time, a lifetime annuity can protect you from outliving your retirement savings. The trade-off is access: That money is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security.

An annuity is neither a bond nor cash. It works as an insurance contract: you pay an insurance company in exchange for income. An immediate annuity starts paying within a year of purchase, while a deferred annuity starts at a later date. Money in a 401(k) or IRA that is invested in stocks can grow over time and help keep pace with inflation. Annuity income is usually fixed, so it can lose purchasing power as prices rise unless you add an inflation adjustment or rider, but that protection also comes at a price: a lower initial payout. Annuity fees can be as much as 10% of the value of your contract. Surrender charges can be substantial if you withdraw money early.

But I have some questions: I understand why the prospect of $40,000 in guaranteed annual income is tempting. If payments continued for those periods, you would collect $400,000 over 10 years, $800,000 over 20 years and potentially $1.2 million over 30 years. Make sure you read the fine print. Is that $40,000 guaranteed income for one person's lifetime? Or is it for both of your lifetimes? Does the surviving spouse continue to receive the full $40,000-a-year income? Is there a death benefit or return-of-premium provision or rider if one spouse dies? Last but not least, are the $40,000-a-year payments adjusted for inflation?

Don't miss: My wife and I are in our 70s. Should we pay off our 2.5% mortgage or invest in a stock market driven by AI?

Investing in the stock market

Third, the pros of leaving the money in the stock market: If you left your $400,000 invested for another 10 years instead of putting it into an annuity, it could grow to approximately $592,000 at an annual return of 4%, $787,000 at 7%, or $864,000 at 8%. These estimates assume annual compounding, with investment earnings reinvested, and exclude taxes, fees and additional contributions. The biggest difference between this scenario and the option of buying an annuity with your $400,000 is that the former is not guaranteed. You are potentially giving up the prospect of a larger return in exchange for security.

An annuity and a trust provide different estate-planning functions. Annuities distribute your assets per the terms of the contract, whereas a trust is designed to manage, protect and distribute your estate during your lifetime and beyond. As this guide on Estate Guru points out, trusts and annuities solve different estate-planning problems: (1) Bypassing probate or buying an annuity isn't an estate plan. (2) A trust can manage your assets if you become incapacitated, provide for minor children or beneficiaries with special needs, address the complications of a blended family and set out the conditions for an inheritance.

Revocable living trusts can benefit people with modest estates, particularly those seeking to avoid probate or plan for incapacity. For families with complicated estates, putting accounts and assets under a single trustee can keep everything running smoothly. It can also help prevent conflicts involving beneficiary designations. Marital trusts matter most in blended families, where each spouse wants to be sure their own children are provided for if the other dies. A special-needs trust can supplement government benefits, while a spendthrift trust can prevent beneficiaries from selling or using their future inheritance as collateral for a loan.

Know what you're buying, and be sure you're doing it for the right reasons.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group, where members help answer life's thorniest money issues. Post your questions, weigh in on the latest Moneyist columns or email The Moneyist at qfottrell@marketwatch.com.

-Quentin Fottrell

data.title: The surprising reason the U.S. economy is speeding up - and might have more room to run
data.description:
By Jeffry Bartash

The main engine of U.S. growth is in overdrive

The U.S. economy is entering its seventh year of expansion and shows little sign of slowing down. It can thank the American consumer.

The U.S. economy is staring at lots of obstacles, but relentless household spending suggests a post-COVID expansion now entering its seventh year has more room to run.

Consumer spending, the main engine of the economy, was astonishingly strong in the spring and summer. And it's shown little sign of sputtering toward year-end, even though surveys show Americans aren't very happy.

A snapshot of U.S. retail sales in October offers the latest proof of the remarkable endurance of the economy. Although the headline increase in sales last month was modest, the details of the retail report were much stronger.

Sales at online stores, for example, surged for the third month in a row and hinted at a strong holiday shopping season.

Spending at restaurants has also been on the rise, in a sign Americans feel confident in the economy. Restaurant sales have risen 7% in the past 12 months, marking the fastest rate of growth in three years even after adjusting for inflation.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's GDPNow forecast estimates the U.S. economy is on track to grow more than 3% in the final three months of 2026, after a frothy 3.4% increase in the third quarter. Gross domestic product is the official scorecard of sorts for the economy.

Senior Federal Reserve officials also recognized the positive vibes. They recently upgraded their view of economic growth to "strong" from "solid," the description they used in the first nine months of the year.

Faster spending

The rise in consumer spending is not simply a result of higher prices. Spending surged at a 3.8% annual pace in both the second and third quarters even after subtracting for inflation.

Those were the biggest back-to-back quarterly increases in almost two years - and well above the 2.5% quarterly average since 2001.

Larger-than-usual tax refunds played a big role in consumer spending in the spring. Big stock-market gains - the so-called wealth effect - have also played a large part. Wealthier households sold or borrowed against those assets to buy new cars and to handle other expenses.

Some economists contend the U.S. has become too reliant on what they call a "K-shaped" economy - where higher-income households are doing well while everyone else struggles.

Yet the most recent data from Bank of America Institute found the gap in credit-card spending between wealthier and less wealthy households had closed considerably. Everyone, it seems, is spending more.

What gives? Mike Reid, head of economics at RBC, credits a stable labor market in which layoffs and the unemployment rate (4.1%) are extremely low. Good job security means consumers don't have to cut back.

"When most people who want a job have one, they will continue to spend their incomes," Reid said.

What will also help in the final two months of the year are lower gas prices. They've declined 13% in the past month and are likely to keep falling.

Stephen Stanley, chief U.S. economist at Santander Capital Markets, said households are likely to save some of the money from lower fuel costs, but they'll also use the extra cash to buy other goods and services.

"The consumer at the moment seems rock solid," Stanley said. "A pullback in energy costs should help to sustain the vigor seen in consumer spending so far this year."

Bumps and roadblocks

Even if consumers keep the pedal to the metal, economists say they are bound to slow their spending to some extent, most likely after the holiday shopping season.

High gas prices and high inflation, for instance, have forced households to dip into their savings. They'll have to replenish their bank accounts eventually.

What's more, a big drop in the stock market this month could dull the edges of the wealth effect. The boom in artificial intelligence fueled a huge run-up in stocks in the past few years, but now investors are nervous.

The S&P 500 SPX, for instance, has lost more than 7% of its value in the past few weeks.

Lower-income households, meanwhile, are still under lots of stress. Their incomes have fallen behind inflation recently and they don't have much of a financial cushion.

"The drop in gas prices in November will help free up some much-needed cash this holiday season, but middle-class and moderate-income households are feeling the strain," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union.

The stress is evident in late credit payments. Elizabeth Renter, lead economist at Life360, said the share of credit-card balances that are "seriously delinquent is the highest it's been since 2011."

One telltale sign of softening consumer demand would be a sharp slowdown in restaurant spending. People tend to cook more at home and eat out less if they're worried about their job or the economy.

So far, there's no sign of it. Spending at bars and restaurants has risen steadily since the spring, and sales are expected to be robust through the holiday season.

"Dining out remains a priority," said Jeffrey Roach, chief economist at LPL Financial in Charlotte, N.C.

-Jeffry Bartash

data.title: Anthropic IPO Fails to Bring Broader Boost to Stocks
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Stocks are down despite a record-setting IPO from Anthropic.

All three major indexes were down mid-afternoon. The Dow led the decline, falling 1.4%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were both down 1.1%.

Anthropic started trading on public markets at $111.50, more than 30% ahead of the price it set Wednesday night. The offering is the biggest of all time.

However, concerns about tech spending, AI-related export controls and Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang's exit last week are continuing to weigh on sentiment. Nvidia was down 1%, while Coreweave fell 3.8%.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: L&D Importance Outpaces Reported Effectiveness: McLean & Company's New Guide Addresses Learning Decision Ownership
data.description:
L&D Importance Outpaces Reported Effectiveness: McLean & Company's New Guide Addresses Learning Decision Ownership

L&D Importance Outpaces Reported Effectiveness: McLean & Company's New Guide Addresses Learning Decision Ownership

PR Newswire

TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026

Who decides which learning initiatives deserve time and resources? Global HR research and advisory firm McLean & Company's new guide outlines how learning and development governance can clarify approval responsibilities and keep learning priorities focused on achieving organizational goals.

TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- McLean & Company's newly published Guide to Establishing Learning and Development Governance outlines how HR leaders can decide which learning initiatives take priority within their organization, who approves them, and how decisions are reviewed. The global HR research and advisory firm says clear ownership and consistent processes can improve the speed and scalability of learning and development (L&D) delivery and align learning investments with organizational priorities. The guide defines the policies, processes, and structures that connect an established learning strategy to decisions about what the organization delivers. HR leaders can use that basis to ensure each learning decision supports organizational priorities and measurable outcomes.

An established L&D strategy sets the direction for learning, while governance connects that direction to execution by identifying where decisions sit, who is accountable, and how decisions will be reviewed. According to McLean & Company insights, organizational needs, priorities, and desired outcomes provide the basis for deciding which learning activities require oversight.

"Governance should make learning decisions easier, not add another layer of administration," says Leann Schneider, director, HR Research & Advisory Services, at McLean & Company. "The goal is to make ownership visible, involve the right people, and create practical routes from a learning request to a well-supported decision. The framework must also fit the organization. A model that works for a smaller, centralized team may not suit a complex enterprise."

The Guide to Establishing Learning and Development Governance from McLean & Company organizes the work into four practical areas for HR leaders, outlined below:

  1. Identify the decisions that require governance. This area helps HR leaders use the L&D strategy to pinpoint decisions involving strategic direction, design and quality, delivery and localization, and measurement and improvement.
     
  2. Define a decision structure. Next, they'll determine whether decisions should be centralized, decentralized, or shared and assign clear accountability and roles for input, approval, and execution.
     
  3. Establish governance processes. From there, leaders put in place consistent intake, prioritization, execution, and escalation mechanisms that make demand, trade-offs, and follow-through visible.
     
  4. Operationalize and sustain the framework. Finally, the framework stays current through a regular review cadence, visibility into learning decisions, stronger collaboration, and success measures that refine governance as needs change.

In the guide, McLean & Company encourages CHROs and other HR department leaders to tailor L&D governance to their organization's size, structure, and complexity rather than apply one model universally. For example, less complex organizations may be well served by governance led directly by HR or L&D, while complex organizations may need a cross-functional council. Matching participants and oversight to each learning decision allows leaders to establish clear ownership while keeping governance practical.

data.title: AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of Stewart Title Guaranty de México, S.A. de C.V.
data.description:
AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of Stewart Title Guaranty de México, S.A. de C.V.

AM Best has affirmed the Financial Strength Rating of A- (Excellent), the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “a-” (Excellent) and the Mexico National Scale Rating of “aaa.MX” (Exceptional) of Stewart Title Guaranty de México, S.A. de C.V. (STGM) (Mexico). The outlook of these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable.

STGM is a member of Stewart Title Group (Stewart), which on a consolidated basis has a balance sheet strength that AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management.

The ratings also reflect the integration of STGM into its parent company, Stewart Title Guaranty Company (STGC) (Houston, TX), and into the group in terms of business model and operational support.

In addition to Mexico, STGC offers products through its subsidiaries to markets in the United States, the European Union, Australia, Costa Rica and China. Given the specialized nature of the title insurance product and the institutional strategy, STGM’s sales efforts focus on business referred by STGC on existing customers, which generates a limited number of policies per year.

The company has experienced a downward growth trend in its capital and surplus, driven by dividend payments from accumulated retained earnings. Support from STGC in the past has come through capital injections, with the most recent one in 2012, directed to help strengthen the business when required.

STGM’s book of business contracted for fourth consecutive year, presenting negative bottom line results driven by significant reduction in the gross written premium. However, the company is implementing an expense reduction plan to offset these impacts.

For year-end 2026, AM Best expects STGM to maintain its operating performance assessment level, supported by its referred business system. Although negative results are anticipated, investment income and a contained expense reduction are expected to help the operation of the company.

Negative rating action could occur if challenges from high interest rates and a slowing economy result in a significant decline in operating profitability or a material decline in risk-adjusted capitalization levels.

This press release relates to Credit Ratings that have been published on AM Best’s website. data.title: GIVE THE GIFT OF IMAGINATION AND INSPIRATION THIS HOLIDAY SEASON WITH A TOUR OF JIM HENSON'S CREATURE SHOP IN NEW YORK
data.description:
GIVE THE GIFT OF IMAGINATION AND INSPIRATION THIS HOLIDAY SEASON WITH A TOUR OF JIM HENSON'S CREATURE SHOP IN NEW YORK

GIVE THE GIFT OF IMAGINATION AND INSPIRATION THIS HOLIDAY SEASON WITH A TOUR OF JIM HENSON'S CREATURE SHOP IN NEW YORK

PR Newswire

QUEENS, N.Y., Nov. 19, 2026

Holiday-Themed Printable Card with Special Video
Delivered with Tickets and Gift Vouchers for a Limited Time

Creature Shop Pop-Up Store Open to Public Every Week

Dates on Sale Through March 2027

Popular sell-out tours feature puppetry and puppet-building demonstrations,
exclusive merch, photo ops, and more!

QUEENS, N.Y., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This holiday season, a truly memorable gift that celebrates imagination, inspiration, and artistry can be found at Jim Henson's Creature Shop in Queens, NY, where weekly tours of this iconic puppet workshop are on sale now through March of 2027. (Visit www.JimHensonExperiences.com for tickets and info.) And just for the holidays, any tickets or gift vouchers purchased before the end of the year will feature a special printable card and video to add some extra "Henson-y" fun to this special gift.

Launched in February 2026, tours of Jim Henson's Creature Shop have been selling out as both visitors and locals discover this unique opportunity to see in person the craft and performance that goes into creating the world's most famous puppet characters. The tour includes a walk-through of the award-winning Creature Shop, special photo opportunities of beloved and iconic characters, a puppetry demonstration from an actual Henson puppeteer, a meet and greet with one of the Creature Shop's master puppet builders, and other special surprises.

On tour days, the public is also welcome to visit the Creature Shop's pop-up shop which includes exclusive merch, collectibles, apparel, and the popular "Scrap Bags" that feature real fabric, fleece, and fur from our Shop projects.

With multiple five-star reviews, and celebrity visits from Al Roker, Marshawn Lynch, and more, tours of Jim Henson's Creature Shop have become a must-see. This holiday season, they are the perfect gift for an enjoyable outing with family or friends, a memorable date night, or a surprise for that special fan of Jim Henson and his legacy.

Jim Henson's Creature Shop is where award-winning artists and makers create hundreds of the world's most famous puppet characters including stars from Fraggle Rock, The Muppet Show, Sesame Street, Emmet Otter's Jug-Band Christmas, and many more. New York City is the original and longest home to the workshop and specializes in the renowned Henson style of puppets and walkaround characters. 

Tickets to visit Jim Henson's Creature Shop in New York are $150 (plus tax and fees). All available dates are on sale now at www.JimHensonExperiences.com, a new initiative from The Jim Henson Company that features a variety of in-person experiences and live theater productions. Join the newsletter to receive updates on all the Company's events, stage shows, and experiences.

About Jim Henson's Creature Shop
Jim Henson's Creature Shop™ provides animatronic creatures, digital puppetry, and soft puppets to the international film, television, theater, live event and advertising industries. Recent credits include the PBS KIDS special Wowsabout, the wildly popular music video "A Boggart Ballad" for Magic: The Gathering, Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock (Apple TV), for which it won an Emmy, The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance (Netflix), the Blumhouse horror franchise Five Nights at Freddy's, and the all-puppet episode of Star Trek: Strange New Worlds. The Shop is renowned for designing and building some of the world's best-known characters including the Sesame Street puppets, the classic Muppets, and characters from Dinosaurs, Farscape, The Dark Crystal, Labyrinth, and more. Additional credits in film and television include The Naked Gun, Nine Perfect Strangers Season 2, Lost Ollie, Come Play, Julie's Greenroom, and Where the Wild Things Are. The shop is also known for its performance work for theatrical productions including My Neighbour Totoro, Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, Jim Henson's Inspired Silliness, and Emmet Otter's Jug-Band Christmas, as well as for its partnerships with commercial clients like Snuggle, Topgolf, and General Mills, and with artists like Coldplay, The Avett Brothers, Cee Lo Green, Ben Rector, Lady Gaga and Deadmau5.

A recipient of multiple Emmy Awards for its outstanding work building puppets for Sesame Street, the Shop also received an Academy Award for its visual effects work on the film Babe. Other awards include a Scientific and Engineering Academy Award for the Henson Performance Control System, a powerful custom-based interface for puppeteers, and an Emmy Award for its work in developing the Henson Digital Puppetry Studio, a patented control system technology that enables puppeteers to perform a computer generated (CG) character in real time.

Vehicle Management Solutions Selected by Colorado Department of Transportation for Safety Patrol Services

Vehicle Management Solutions (“VMS” or the “Company”), a portfolio company of Mill Point Capital LLC (“Mill Point”), today announced that its Safety Service Patrol (“SSP”) division has been selected by the Colorado Department of Transportation (“CDOT”) to support its Safety Patrol program. The contract marks a significant expansion of VMS’s national SSP footprint and reinforces its position as a leading provider of traffic incident management services to state transportation agencies.

Under the contract, VMS will deploy a comprehensive SSP program designed to improve incident clearance times, reduce secondary crashes, enhance roadside safety for motorists and first responders and minimize congestion impacts across Colorado’s highway network. The program will leverage VMS’ experience, personnel and technology platform to deliver coordinated field response, training and performance tracking across CDOT’s network.

“Colorado represents an important milestone as we continue expanding our SSP programs nationwide,” said Kevin Corcoran, CEO of VMS. “By combining deep operational expertise with purpose-built technology, we are committed to helping CDOT keep roadways safer and traffic moving efficiently.”

About Vehicle Management Solutions
Headquartered in Tinley Park, IL, VMS is a leading provider of end-to-end vehicle management solutions including dispatch, vehicle storage and traffic incident management. VMS’s mission is to keep streets, roads and highways moving safely and efficiently. With a nationwide presence, VMS focuses on building long-term relationships with states, municipalities, law enforcement agencies, insurance companies, logistics companies and various other clients to serve their communities. For more information, please visit www.vmsolutions.com.
